title: Attribute-driven roleset and assertion policies for RBAC v2
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Goal: design an attribute-driven roleset and assertion policy layer for RBAC v2 that unifies resource-hierarchy bindings, SSO/SAML assertions, and audit-friendly decision trails. The new model should support: 1) declarative attribute -> role bindings (user attributes, group assertions, certificate SANs), 2) scoped role instances tied to resource nodes in the hierarchy, 3) deny/allow priority rules and breakglass overrides for emergency admin actions, and 4) compact event records that include assertion provenance for audit logs. This ticket focuses on the data model, matching algorithm, and compatibility constraints for existing role resolution codepaths.
acceptance_criteria: Spec + sequence diagrams describing attribute mapping, evaluation order, and decision provenance
JSON schema for roleset, attribute-binding, and assertion metadata that can be stored in config-service
Compatibility shim that can interpret legacy role-assignments and co-exist with new attribute bindings
Unit tests covering evaluation for: direct role grants, attribute-derived grants, group-assertion grants, deny precedence, and temporary breakglass elevation
Audit record spec with required fields (principal, token_id, assertion_source, evaluation_trace, effective_permissions) and example payloads
design_decisions: Primary index model: use (resource_path, role_id, scope_type) triple for fast lookup. Resource paths are slash-delimited and support prefix queries for ancestor inheritance.

Attribute model: accept three attribute sources - identity provider assertions (SAML/OIDC group/claims), internal user attributes (profile, tags), and ephemeral session attributes (MFA, context) - with configurable weights.

Evaluation order: explicit denies -> direct role grants -> attribute-derived grants -> inherited grants from ancestor resources -> breakglass overrides (recorded and time-limited). Deny always wins except when a signed breakglass token is present.
Assertion provenance: every granted permission must include an assertion_source field (e.g., idp:saml:ACME:idp_group:eng-admin) to support downstream audit queries and forensics.

Backward compat: introduce a compatibility flag 'convertible' on legacy bindings so migration tooling can generate equivalent attribute bindings without changing runtime semantics immediately. New resolver will consult legacy map when flag present.

Storage: roleset and attribute bindings live in config-service with optimistic concurrency, and a precomputed evaluation cache stores flattened effective-roles for high-read tenants; cache invalidation hooks are keyed by binding id and resource path prefixes.
tradeoffs: Complexity vs expressivity: attribute-driven bindings allow flexible SAML mappings (e.g., nested groups, claim transforms) but complicate evaluation; mitigated via precomputation for hot paths.

Cache staleness vs immediacy: aggressive precomputation reduces latency for permission checks but requires robust invalidation; decided to accept a 2s eventual window for Dedicated/Hosted control planes and provide a strict mode for Private customers who require synchronous updates.

Deny semantics: the chosen deny-first model minimizes accidental privilege escalation but requires careful deny-rule scoping (deny-too-broad could block admin recovery); so breakglass tokens with audit-only early warning are part of the design.

Audit payload size: recording full evaluation traces aids forensics but increases storage and indexing costs; propose tiered retention (full-trace for 90 days, compact snapshot thereafter) configurable per customer.
Migration difficulty: conversion of hundreds of existing tenant bindings is nontrivial; we will ship an automated converter plus a migrate-in-stages plan instead of a hard cutover.
tasks: Write JSON schema for attribute-binding and roleset (ENG: schema and examples)
Create sequence diagrams for evaluation flow and assertion provenance
Prototype resolver that accepts SAML assertions and maps to temporary role grants
Implement audit event structure and add to runtime logging pipeline
Add config-service endpoints and validate optimistic concurrency model
Design migration tooling and a dry-run converter for existing role assignments
E2E tests: unit resolver tests and integration test with SAML idp emulator
